reason: The hypothesis cites no prior evidence (supporting_evidence_ids is empty). All key premises—formation of a protective oxide on Q235, its barrier mechanism, high-temperature stability, and quantitative corrosion reduction—are specific claims requiring experimental support, which is absent.
premises: Chemical oxidation can produce a dense, adherent iron oxide layer on Q235 steel
Such an oxide layer acts as a barrier limiting oxygen/moisture ingress and anodic dissolution
Barrier properties are retained at elevated temperature (~100°C) despite enhanced ion diffusion
Barrier effect translates to lower corrosion rate, less pitting, and higher impedance in chloride environments
